chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who went out with a bird from Makkah to Al-Kufa. He said: 'He should return it to Makkah'.

key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Al-Kufa, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.طَيْرٍ: Bird, specifically in the context of hunting or game
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the holy city and center of Al-Haram
key_terms.يَرُدُّهُ: He should return it, indicating a legal obligation of restitution or relocation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a bird taken out of Makkah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurarah, clarifies the procedural aspect of expiation (kaffarah) for hunting within the sacred precincts of Makkah. It establishes that the hunted bird itself is returned to the Haram, reinforcing the concept that the sanctity of the land extends to its fauna and that the penalty involves restoring the specific item taken from the holy boundary.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Musna Al Hannat, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who went out with a bird, from Makkah to Al-Kufa. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should return it to Makkah’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Muthanna’ al-Hannat from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who leaves Makkah with a bird for al-Kufah. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must return it to Makkah.’”
